title: SUNI architecture
note: A prototype over four subsystems. The other nine lanes of the flat page are not in here yet.

groups.title: Tiered models
groups.lead: Which brain answers, decided before a brain is asked

items.title: direct_to_claude_code(text) → bool
items.lead: ~0 ms · regex only · no LLM call
body: Code / system patterns → T5 bypass
_SUNI_TOOLS_RE exclusion: email / KB / memory
RBAC gate: claude_task not blocked · not read-only
False-negative safe: local fallback always available

items.title: complexity_score(text) → 1–4
items.lead: Word count + keyword signals → starting tier
body: Simple: T1 · Multi-step: T2 · Complex: T3 · Long: T4
Capped at system_profile.MAX_LOCAL_TIER
Selects tier for OllamaAgent loop

items.title: needs_escalation(response) → bool
items.lead: Post-response escalation signal
body: "I cannot" / "beyond my capabilities" → next tier
Short hedging (<60 words) → retry
T4 = local ceiling — no further escalation

items.title: model_inventory.py
items.lead: Ollama network scanner — runs at startup
body: Queries each endpoint in config.ollama_endpoints
params_to_tier() → T1–T4 assignment
Cached · GET /api/models/inventory (admin)
?refresh=1 forces rescan

items.title: system_profile.py
items.lead: VRAM detection at startup
body: nvidia-smi → available VRAM
Sets MAX_LOCAL_TIER + DEFAULT_TIER
RTX 4000 8 GB → T2 default, T2 max local

items.title: ClaudeCodeAgent
items.lead: suni/models/claude_code_agent.py
body: Registered as T5 if `claude` in PATH
CLAUDE_API_KEY_CTX per-user injection
--resume session_id persisted per-conversation (conversations.db)
cwd=~ + --system-prompt → isolated SUNI persona, no project leak
Every task: KB index path (doc_meta.json) + your document folders direct-read hint
Every turn folds Tier 2a/2b memory + lang context · _run_claude() · _parse_json_output()

Prompt via real-file stdin · final answer read from -o

items.lead: suni/core/orchestrate.py · opt-in conv_mode
body: DRAFT (all models ∥) → CROSS-CRITIQUE (peer-review ∥) → SYNTHESISE (1 merges, speaks as SUNI)
Decorrelated frontier pool (Claude Code + Codex, admin-editable)
Live phase events (draft·critique·synthesize) · fast/full dial
Self-contained branch in _run_inner — Mode 1 pipeline untouched
power-user/admin only · cloud (data leaves box) · per-message toggle

items.lead: factory.make_provider_agent(provider, …)
body: ollama · vllm · openai · anthropic · gemini · claude-code · codex
Both auth modes: API keys AND no-key subscription CLIs
Admin drag-ordered model chain · collaborate pool

groups.title: Named agents
groups.lead: A saved way to be, and a way to be asked again tomorrow

items.title: Agent Profiles
items.lead: A prompt, an optional model, an optional narrowing of tools
body: Stored as Markdown + YAML frontmatter beside a SQLite index, so a
definition stays readable and editable outside the app
Sharing mirrors project_members: owner / editor / viewer
Model pinned by a profile suppresses tier escalation — otherwise the choice would be swapped out mid-run
routes_to_cli() makes the pin decide the PATH too: force_claude_code used to route
before the tier loop was reached, so a pinned agent went to the CLI anyway and the
cheap specialist cost what the expensive one does. "claude-code" pins the CLI in reverse.
A profile naming an UNREGISTERED tool is warned about: the intersection
keeps the name, the registry returns nothing, and the model narrates
instead of calling — which reads as a weak model and is not

items.title: Narrowing, never widening
items.lead: Tools & MCP INTERSECT with the caller's role; blocks UNION
body: Re-derived every run, never stored — AGENT.md is a file a user can edit
A profile cannot grant a conversation mode the role lacks
Without this an admin-authored agent in a dropdown would be privilege escalation for whoever picked it

items.title: Deterministic intent
items.lead: Cadence, delivery and agent parsed by regex, not chosen by the model
body: Measured: at the core tier the same prompt picked four different wrong
tools across four runs, with the right one registered and hinted
Missing detail is ASKED for, never invented
No capable local tier → automatic escalation to T5

items.title: Scheduled Invocations
items.lead: Replays a PROMPT through the orchestrator, not an OS command
body: Runs as the owner, role read AT FIRE TIME — not a snapshot, which would
preserve permissions the owner has since lost
Delivery performed by the runner: unattended runs have no approver, so
the model never chooses a recipient
Unknown cadence refused, never rounded · missed slots do not stack
A failure used to do exactly what a success did — write the status and wait for the next
slot, so a job whose password expired failed every morning for as long as nobody read the
list. Now: one retry five minutes later, then DISABLED with the reason on the record.
Disabled, not deleted: the owner has to see it and switch it back on. A success clears the streak.

items.title: Delegation
items.lead: "Ask the X agent to…" hands the task to that agent
body: The NAME is extracted by regex, not chosen by the model — measured, the
core tier picked four different wrong tools across four runs
Sub-turn grants intersect the CALLING turn's, not the raw role, or a
narrow agent delegates its way back to full reach
An agent that DECLARES tools is floored at a tier that can emit
well-formed calls, and escalates to T5 when no local tier qualifies — a
pinned model is never overridden
Depth cap 1: agents may be invoked, may not invoke · unknown name refused, never self-handled

items.title: Panel Agents
items.lead: An agent whose model is a PANEL, not a model
body: Draft → cross-critique → synthesise across the pool, answered in
that agent's voice. Per-agent pool override
Persona shapes only the SYNTHESIS — applying it to every seat would
correlate the models, which is the whole point of a panel
Cloud models: this leaves the machine, unlike the single-model path

items.title: Ceilings
items.lead: The instance cap bounds one turn; these bound a day of them
body: A schedule firing every 15 minutes has no natural stopping point
max_steps applies as a MINIMUM against the instance cap — a profile can
tighten it, never raise it, the same rule as its tool grants
A run count is a poor proxy for spend: one turn that delegates to the CLI
and reads forty documents costs orders of magnitude more than a one-line
reply, and both counted as one run — hence a TOKEN ceiling beside it
Runs and tokens both counted from the audit trail, not a profile counter that would drift on a failed run
The CLI reported no tokens at all until its usage was booked (cache reads included) — every budget read zero on the path that spends most: "say only: ready" costs ~26k input tokens

items.title: Fan-out
items.lead: Ask several specialists at once, then answer as the head
body: Each one runs the ORDINARY request path with its own profile, so grants,
model pins and daily ceilings all still apply — the fan-out decides who
is asked, never what they may do
Skipped and failed agents reach the composer BY NAME: an answer built
from two of five must not read like an answer from five
fanout_token_budget is checked BEFORE each specialist starts, against what the turn has already spent — an expensive first answer stops the rest instead of being noticed afterwards
Measured 2026-09-26: with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2, one generation 57 tok/s, two at once 88 tok/s aggregate. With one slot they merely queue.

items.title: Assignments
items.lead: Work handed to an agent that outlives the request asking for it
body: The caller gets the record back at once; the agent works through the
ordinary path and the result waits, with a notification if configured
A task lives in SQLite but RUNS in memory, so a stopped process left rows claiming "running" with nothing running them — interrupted work is failed at startup instead

items.title: Why the work exists
items.lead: A delegated or scheduled run starts from a bare instruction in a fresh context
body: The specialist is handed "summarise the Q3 numbers" with no hint that a
board pack is being assembled, and a job firing every Monday cannot tell
a first attempt from a fourth
The originating request travels with the delegation; a scheduled run is
told that it recurs and how the last attempt went
Background, not instruction — and it says so in itself, because a reply that narrates SUNI's plumbing is a bug this codebase has already shipped once

items.title: Preview before trust
items.lead: What it WOULD call, and what it may reach — executing nothing
body: Reports the resolved grants too: what an agent could reach is the
governance question, and another task might choose differently
Unlike task mode, the plan is NOT stashed — an executable plan left behind turns a preview into something one word could fire

items.title: Traceable by agent
items.lead: Which agent answered, and what it was allowed to reach then
body: Per-request row carries agent_slug; a governance event records the
RESOLVED grants — model, mode, tool count, MCP prefixes
Grants are re-derived each run, so the profile as it stands later is not evidence of what applied
report(slug, days) reads it back — what it DID vs what it COULD reach,
identical grant states collapsed because only a change is signal

groups.title: The field
groups.lead: Everything she can reach, as one navigable graph

items.title: One level per request
items.lead: A view, never a second source of truth — every node is something another part of SUNI already owns
body: 7,637 indexed files across 2,304 folders: sending that as a graph is
megabytes for a picture nobody can read, so a request asks about one
focus and gets its children, the way a directory listing does
Children are capped and the remainder becomes one "+N more" node —
a view that quietly omits things is worse than one that says so
Nothing here reads the filesystem: folders come from the document index, so this cannot become a way to enumerate a disk SUNI was never pointed at
Neighbours are the OS's own ARP cache and nothing else — the test for that checks what the code CALLS, after an earlier version passed on the word "pings" in a docstring

items.title: Drawn, not pasted over
items.lead: Raw WebGL on the Face's own context — a second context for the same canvas fails
body: Lit spheres that write depth, so the head occludes what is behind it;
additive halos were why the palette washed out
Names appear by DRAWN SIZE, so zooming in names more of them, overlaps
are dropped rather than nudged, and nothing lands on her face
Grouping lays the categories out on a disc facing the viewer: a sphere puts half of them edge-on and forces the camera so far back that every node becomes a dot
One icon flickered and no other: its atlas index sat exactly on a row boundary, where floor(4.0/4.0) at mediump returns 0 about half the time. The cell is worked out in the vertex stage now.

items.title: She can point at it
items.lead: Asked which devices are on the network, the picture goes there and the words come from the same read
body: The tool returns the node list as TEXT as well, so Telegram, a schedule
and the API get a working answer with no picture to move
Recognised deterministically before the turn starts, in both languages:
the local tier was offered the tool, described it, and did not call it —
the same measurement that drove schedules and named agents
A view change is not consequential: an approval card in front of every "mostra-me a rede" is a feature nobody uses twice
With neighbour discovery off it SAYS so and names the setting, rather than showing an empty view to someone with eighteen machines on their LAN

items.title: Opening a file from a picture
items.lead: Three locks, because a file read through a graph is still a file read
body: The caller's ROLE must be allowed the knowledge base; the path must be
IN the index matched on its real path; every open writes an AUDIT row
/api/files/serve could not be reused: it serves the caller's own output
and uploads, and widening it to reach the archive would have widened it
for every account at once
The index is system-wide and single, so being in it is NOT a per-user permission — gating on membership alone hands every scanned file to the most restricted account
Being under an indexed FOLDER is not enough either: that includes everything the scanner deliberately skipped

items.title: Back is not up
items.lead: The breadcrumb says where a level SITS; back says where the viewer WAS
body: A drive's parent is the knowledge base whatever route you took, so from
the overview — where everything is one click away — climbing the trail
lands somewhere never visited
Opening a drive skips folders holding exactly one thing; the trail went
on offering every skipped folder as its own step, and all of them
resolved back to the folder on screen
Clicking the centre sphere goes back. It is drawn from buffer index 0 and is in no node list, so picking could never return it — the most obvious target on screen did nothing at all.

items.title: Controls that can be reached
items.lead: Three of them were in the DOM, bound to handlers, and unreachable
body: The page hides a control with opacity 0 and pointer-events none and
reveals it with a class. Nothing errors when the class never arrives:
the button exists, the handler is bound, the click never happens
One was toggled nowhere; one only when a level loaded, which is not
when focus changes; one had its opacity restored and not its
pointer-events, so it was visible, hover-styled and untouchable
A keyboard shortcut was the wrong shape entirely: the chat box takes focus on load and after every reply, so a bare letter never reaches the handler
The regression guard for it passed while the bug was present. It matched any toggle in the function rather than each element's own — now each of the three bugs, reinstated, fails it.

edges.note: the router picks a tier, the factory builds the agent
a named agent runs the ordinary request path under its profile
a profile's pinned model decides the path, not just the tier
show_network moves the view through the event channel
the agents level lists the caller's own profiles and schedules
